info.title: Build Canada Data API
info.summary: Cited, reproducible public data on Canadian governments, organizations and federal spending.
info.description:
Read-only access to everything fact-factory publishes: the entity registry
(jurisdictions, government organizations, Indigenous governments, charities and other
organizations), their identifiers, relationships and lineage, and federal spending
rows linked to them.

Three rules shape the API:

1. **Every fact carries its citation.** Fact-bearing objects have `provenance` (the
   asset, release, pinned snapshot, captured file and row) and a ready-to-paste `cite`.
2. **Every answer is reproducible.** Pass `as_of=<release>` and the same URL returns the
   same bytes forever. Omit it and the response names the release it used.
3. **Caveats are data.** `meta.caveats[]` carries machine-readable warnings, such as
   `not_cross_source_total`. Act on them. Amounts from different spending sources
   overlap: never add them.

Conventions: responses are `{data, meta, links}`; lists use cursor pagination
(`limit`, `cursor`, `meta.next_cursor`); errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`
with a stable `code`; money is a decimal string with an ISO 4217 `currency`; IDs are
`gid://buildcanada/<Type>/<key>`. Each operation's cost in request units is in
`x-bc-units`; each data field names its data dictionary term in `x-bc-dictionary`.

No key is needed to start: anonymous callers get 30 units a minute and 1,000 a day
with the read:public scope. Get a free key at https://auth.buildcanada.com/developers.
Agents: start at https://data.buildcanada.com/llms.txt, or connect the MCP server at
https://data.buildcanada.com/mcp.

license.name: API responses carry each source's licence; Build Canada's own data is OGL-Canada-2.0

get.description:
The front door. Names the latest release and links to every collection, the OpenAPI
document, the docs, llms.txt and the MCP server. Start here, or at
https://data.buildcanada.com/llms.txt.

The OpenAPI 3.1 document for /v1, as JSON. It is the contract: request and response
validation, SDKs, docs and MCP tool schemas are generated from it. Fields name their
data dictionary term in `x-bc-dictionary`; operations give their cost in `x-bc-units`.

Who the API thinks you are: the account and key (or OAuth client), the plan, the
scopes granted and this period's usage. Works anonymously. Use it to check a key
before a long job.

get.summary: Usage by time, key and operation
get.description:
Your account's requests and units by minute, hour or day, optionally split by key and
operation. Past days come from the durable daily rollup (the billing source); the
current day is live and up to a minute behind. Needs the usage:read scope; not
available anonymously.

parameters.name: granularity
parameters.description: Bucket size. `minute` allows at most a 24-hour range; `hour` at most 31 days.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the range (inclusive). Default: 30 days ago for day, 24 hours ago otherwise.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the range (exclusive). Default: now.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: Split buckets by `key`, `operation` or both, comma-separated.

get.summary: Search entities by name or identifier
get.description:
Finds entities by identifier first, then by name. A query that is a BN9, BN15,
corporation number, band number, LEI or census code matches exactly (match.kind
identifier). Otherwise names and aliases match after normalization (exact); with
mode=fuzzy, trigram similarity adds candidates (fuzzy), which are guesses to check,
not matches. There is no address or postal code search. Phase 1 searches entities
only; other types arrive additively.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The name or identifier to find, at least 2 characters.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Result types, comma-separated. Phase 1 has `entity` only.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: `exact` (default) matches identifiers and normalized names; `fuzzy` adds trigram candidates.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Only entities of this class.

parameters.name: jurisdiction
parameters.description: Only entities of this jurisdiction.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Results per page, 1 to 50. Default 20.

200.description: A page of results, best first.

get.summary: Get an entity's predecessors or successors
get.description:
Walks succeeded_by links from the entity: its predecessors (bodies it replaced, such
as the towns amalgamated into it) or successors, nearest first. Lineage is not payment
attribution: a predecessor's spending stays on the predecessor, so ask for each
entity's spending separately.

parameters.description: `predecessors` (default) or `successors`.

parameters.name: max_depth
parameters.description: How many steps to walk, 1 to 10. Default 10.

ApiKey.description: An API key from https://auth.buildcanada.com/developers, sent as `Authorization: Bearer bc_live_…` (`bc_stg_…` on staging). A key carries the scopes its owner granted it (read:public always; read:persons after verification; usage:read by default). Keys are shown once; the console shows only the first 12 characters.

OAuth2.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with PKCE (S256 only; `plain` is refused) and RFC 8707 resource indicators: send `resource=https://data.buildcanada.com/mcp` or `https://data.buildcanada.com/v1`. Clients register by Client ID Metadata Document (preferred) or dynamic client registration at https://auth.buildcanada.com/oauth/register. Access tokens last one hour; refresh tokens rotate. Metadata: https://auth.buildcanada.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

scopes.read:public: Read organizations, spending, releases, datasets, the dictionary and exports.
scopes.read:persons: Read person entities and their public roles (phase 2). Never includes street addresses.
scopes.keys:manage: Create, rotate and revoke API keys (phase 2; OAuth tokens only, never API keys).

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem detail, served as application/problem+json for every error. `type` is a documentation page (with a Markdown twin at the same URL plus `.md`); `code` is the stable machine-readable name to branch on. Members after `code` appear only for the codes that use them. Clients must tolerate new codes and new members.

type.description: URI of the problem type's documentation page, `https://data.buildcanada.com/problems/<code with hyphens>`.

title.description: A short, fixed summary of the problem type. It does not change between occurrences.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated for clients that lose it.

detail.description: What went wrong in this occurrence and what to do next, in plain words.
examples: Key bc_live_7Hq2… used 120 of 120 request units in the current 60-second window.

instance.description: The request ID of the failed request. Quote it in support requests.

code.description: Stable problem code. invalid_parameter (400), unauthenticated (401), insufficient_scope, account_suspended, ip_not_allowed and origin_not_allowed (403), not_found and not_yet_published (404), redirected (301), release_mismatch (409), retired (410), query_too_broad (422), rate_limited and quota_exceeded (429), release_building (503), internal_error (500).

docs.description: The concept page that explains the rule behind this problem.

errors.description: invalid_parameter only. One entry per rejected parameter.

required_scope.description: insufficient_scope only. The scope the operation needs.

retry_after_seconds.description: rate_limited, quota_exceeded and release_building only. Seconds to wait before retrying; equals the Retry-After header.

plan.description: rate_limited and quota_exceeded only. The caller's plan.

upgrade_url.description: rate_limited and quota_exceeded only. Where to raise the limit.

bulk_url.description: rate_limited and quota_exceeded only. Bulk files that answer high-volume needs without the API.

location.description: redirected only. The survivor's URL, equal to the Location header.

earliest_release.description: not_yet_published only. The earliest release the API serves.

cursor_release.description: release_mismatch only. The release the cursor was issued for. Repeat the request with that `as_of`, or drop the cursor.

sunset.description: retired only. The date the operation or field stopped being served.

Meta.title: Meta
Meta.description: Facts about the response itself: which release answered, how `as_of` was resolved, the request ID to quote in support requests, and caveats that apply to the whole response.

release.description: The registry release that answered, or null for data versioned only by time. Pass it back as `as_of` to get the same bytes again.

as_of.description: How the request's `as_of` was resolved, as the release number it pinned (for example "11"), or the timestamp it was evaluated at for time-versioned data. Omitting `as_of` resolves to the latest release, named here.

request_id.description: Identifier of this request. Problem responses repeat it as `instance`.

caveats.description: Caveats that apply to this response. Empty when there are none; never omitted.

ListMeta.title: ListMeta
ListMeta.description: Meta for a paginated list. Adds the cursor for the next page, the page size used and, only when requested with `count=exact`, the total count.

limit.description: The page size used for this page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque, signed cursor for the next page, or null on the last page. It encodes the release, the sort key and the last ID, so it stays valid and stable after a newer release publishes. Pass it as `cursor` with the same other parameters.

count.description: Total matching items. Null unless the request set `count=exact`, which costs 2 more units.

Caveat.title: Caveat
Caveat.description: A machine-readable warning about how to read the data in this response. Agents should act on `code`, not on `text`; `text` is prose for people and follows Accept-Language. Every code has an anchor on https://data.buildcanada.com/docs/caveats. New codes may be added at any time; treat an unknown code as a warning to show the reader.

code.description: Stable caveat code. Known codes include not_cross_source_total, agreement_value_not_paid, latest_revision_only, linked_only, aggregates_excluded, amount_missing, calendar_year_not_fiscal, archive_overlaps_live, coverage_partial, person_is_clustering and observed_not_appointed.

text.description: The caveat in plain words, in the language chosen by Accept-Language.
examples: Sources overlap. Never add amounts across sources.

docs.description: The caveat's documentation anchor, with a Markdown twin at the same URL plus `.md`.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description: Where a fact came from, precisely enough to reproduce it: the fact-factory asset, the release that published it, the pinned Iceberg snapshot for spending, the captured source file and the row in it, the parser version and the licence. Present on every fact-bearing object.

asset.description: The fact-factory asset key that published the fact, such as `sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants` or `entities/entities`. Describe it with GET /v1/datasets/{asset_key}.

release.description: For registry rows, the release that first published this version (dictionary release_id). For spending rows, the release whose pinned snapshot served it.

snapshot_id.description: The Iceberg snapshot the release pinned for this spending table. Null for registry rows.

recorded_at.description: When fact-factory first recorded this version. Not when it became true in the world. Registry rows only.

capture.description: The captured source file, when the fact was parsed from one.

locator.description: Where in the capture the fact is.

source.description: For registry rows, the registry's own record of where this version came from.

parser_version.description: Version of the parsing rules that produced the row. A parser change publishes a new version and keeps the old one.

license.description: The licence the publisher releases the source under, as an SPDX-style identifier such as OGL-Canada-2.0. See the dataset page for attribution wording.

Entity.title: Entity
Entity.description: One party in the Build Canada entity registry, as of the release that answered: a jurisdiction, government organization, government enterprise, Indigenous government or other organization. An entity is Build Canada's record of the party, built from published rosters; its `id` never changes and is never reused. Real-world changes (renames, amalgamations) are lineage (GET /v1/entities/{id}/lineage), not new IDs. A merged duplicate returns 301 to its survivor. `identifiers` and `relationships` are present only when requested with `expand`.

id.description: The entity's global ID. Minted once, never reused.

entity_class.description: What kind of party the entity is.

subtype.description: The class's controlled subtype, such as ministerial_department, municipal_government, first_nation, registered_charity, university, hospital or federal_predecessor. Look terms up with GET /v1/dictionary/subtype.

name.description: The entity's name as its roster publishes it, unchanged.

name_fr.description: The French name, where the roster gives one.

aliases.description: Other names the roster gives for the same entity, such as a legal title or abbreviation. Empty when none.

anchor.description: The roster record the entity was first built from, as `<roster>:<record key>`.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction the entity belongs to. Null when the roster gives none, as for First Nations.

status.description: The roster's own status, such as active, dissolved, inactive, transferred or registered. `not_in_roster` means the roster no longer lists the entity (its ID is kept). `redirected` means another entity now carries its record; see redirected_to.

redirected_to.description: When status is redirected, the survivor that now carries this entity's record. A GET on a redirected entity returns 301 to it.

valid_from.description: When the entity came into existence in the world, at the precision the source gives. Null when the source gives no start.

valid_to.description: When the entity stopped existing in the world, at the precision the source gives. Null when it still exists or the source gives no end; the two are not distinguished. An entity ended by lineage has valid_to set and successors in /lineage.

attributes.description: Roster-specific details, such as institutional_form for federal bodies or category_code for charities. Keys differ by roster and are documented on the dataset page of the entity's provenance asset. Only allowlisted keys are served. Address attributes (such as a school board's `addresses`) are not served in v1.

identifiers.description: The entity's external identifiers. Present only with `expand=identifiers`.

relationships.description: The entity's first 50 outgoing relationships. Present only with `expand=relationships`; page through all of them with /relationships.

links.description: Relative links to the entity's related collections, pinned to the release that answered.

spending.description: Spending rows linked to the entity.

provenance.description: Where this version of the entity came from.

cite.description: A ready-to-paste citation for this entity version, naming the release, the gid and the roster row.
examples: Build Canada entity registry release 11, gid://buildcanada/Entity/01J9ZK4T6M8Q2R5V7X3B1N0C4D; from the Alberta municipal roster, row 212.

SpendingRecord.title: SpendingRecord
SpendingRecord.description: One published row of a federal spending source (a contract, grant, contribution, transfer payment, research award or international project), as the release's pinned Iceberg snapshot holds it, with its typed columns, the source's meaning of `amount`, every party occurrence and whether each is linked to an entity. Rows sharing a canonical_id are revisions of one agreement: never add them together.

id.description: The row's global ID, stable across releases while the source row exists.

is_aggregated.description: True when the row summarizes several recipients or transactions (contracts under $10,000, "Names withheld (10,931 recipients)"). Aggregate rows are left out of summaries and counted in meta.

external_id.description: The source's own identifier for the record, or a hash of the fields that identify it.

canonical_id.description: Groups revisions (amendments) of one agreement. Rows sharing it must not be summed.

source_occurrence.description: 1-based count of how often this record identity has appeared in the same source release. Above 1 means the source repeated it.

acquisition.description: How the capture arrived. archive_import rows come from an external archive and may overlap live rows.

resource_id.description: The source resource (one file or feed) the row came from.

source_row_id.description: The row's id in the published spending table, unique only within one (acquisition, resource_id).

title.description: Short name of the contract, agreement, award or project, in English where the source gives both languages.

description.description: Longer description or summary, in English where the source gives both languages.
examples: Renovation of the Diamond Valley community arts centre.

program.description: Name of the funding program the record belongs to.

payer.description: The English name of the government organization that made the commitment or payment, as the source names it.

payer_code.description: The open.canada.ca organization code of the payer, such as pch. After a reorganization, past rows carry the successor's code.

recipient.description: The recipient as the source names it. Null when the source names no single recipient.

recipients.description: All implementing organizations the source lists (global_affairs_projects only). Empty elsewhere.

recipient_refs.description: The IATI organization identifier of each entry in recipients, at the same position. Empty elsewhere.

principal_investigator.description: The lead researcher named on a research award.

research_org.description: The research institution named on the record, when it is a different party from the recipient.

recipient_business_number.description: The recipient's CRA business number as the source writes it (9-digit BN or 15-character program account).

recipient_type.description: The source's own code for the kind of recipient, unchanged. See the source's notes.

recipient_city.description: City of the recipient, as the source writes it.

recipient_postal_code.description: Postal code of the recipient. For an organization it is the full code as the source writes it, including case and spacing. When the recipient occurrence is an individual (its party's party_kind is individual), only the forward sortation area is served: the first 3 characters, uppercased (for example "T2P"), because people are shown by city, province and FSA only. Bulk files follow the same rule.

province.description: Province or territory of the recipient, as the source writes it.

country.description: Country of the recipient, as the source writes it.

amount.description: The single monetary value that best represents the row. It is not necessarily money paid: `measure` and `amount_note` say what it is for this source. Null when the source gives no single value.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of amount. Null only when amount is null for a mixed-currency project.

measure.description: What amount measures for this source.

amount_note.description: The source's amount rule in plain words, from the data dictionary's per-asset `amount` note.
examples: agreement_value for that amendment. Do not sum across rows sharing a canonical_id.

commitments.description: global_affairs_projects only. Total commitments by currency, from ISO 4217 code to decimal string.

value_consistent.description: proactive_contracts only. Whether contract_value equals original_value plus amendment_value as the source publishes them.

fiscal_year.description: The fiscal year the row belongs to, by the source's rule (see fiscal_year_note on /v1/spending/sources). Null when the source gives no parseable year.

date.description: The row's principal date, such as the contract date or agreement start date, when the source gives it in ISO format.

date_raw.description: The principal date exactly as the source wrote it.

revision_rank.description: Sort key for ordering revisions sharing a canonical_id; higher sorts later. Null when the source has no revision ordering.

is_latest_revision.description: True when this is the highest-ranked revision of its canonical_id, the only revision summaries count.

parties.description: Every party occurrence on the row, with its link outcome. Always present on GET /v1/spending/{id}; in lists only with `expand=parties`.

raw.description: The complete original source record (JSON, or XML for global_affairs_projects). Present only with `expand=raw`. For an individual recipient, the source's postal code field is reduced to its FSA here too, so raw never carries more than the typed columns.

provenance.description: The pinned snapshot, captured file and row this record came from.

cite.description: A ready-to-paste citation naming the publisher, dataset, retrieval date, row, capture digest, release and gid.
examples: Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat, Proactive Disclosure of Grants and Contributions, retrieved 2026-09-26, row 48,213 (sha256 9f2c4e8b). Build Canada data release 11, gid://buildcanada/SpendingRecord/K3M9Q2W7XA4B8C1D5E6F0G2H3J.

Dataset.description: A published fact-factory asset: what one row means, its coverage and freshness, its licence, the dictionary terms its fields use, and where to get it in bulk.

record_meaning.description: What one row is, in plain words, from the data dictionary's per-asset note.

publisher.description: Who publishes the source, or null for assets Build Canada derives.

license.description: The licence the data is available under.

latest_retrieved_at.description: When the newest input the release pinned was retrieved.

from_fiscal_year.description: The earliest fiscal year present, for spending.

to_fiscal_year.description: The latest fiscal year present, for spending.

known_gaps.description: Known gaps against the dictionary definitions, in plain words.

EntityGid.description: Global ID of a registry entity: `gid://buildcanada/Entity/` followed by the entity's 26-character ULID. Minted once and never reused. Paths accept either the bare ULID or the percent-encoded gid.

EntityRef.description: A compact reference to an entity, used where an entity appears inside another object (a relationship's object, a spending party, a lineage step). Fetch the full entity from its `id`.

name.description: The entity's name as its roster publishes it, unchanged.

entity_class.description: What kind of party the entity is.

SearchMatch.description: How a search result matched the query.

matched_on.description: What matched, such as `name`, `alias:<the alias>` or `identifier:<namespace>`.

SearchHit.description: One search result. `match` says how it matched, so an agent can tell a match on an identifier or an exact name from a fuzzy guess. In phase 1 every hit is an entity.

PartialDate.description: A date at the precision the source gives it: a year (`2023`), a year and month (`2023-01`) or a full ISO date (`2023-01-01`). Never padded to a false precision.

Capture.title: Capture
Capture.description: The exact source file a fact was parsed from, as Build Canada retrieved and retained it. The bytes are content-addressed: `url` serves the same bytes forever.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact source bytes.

url.description: Where Build Canada serves the retained bytes, `https://files.buildcanada.com/sha256/<first two characters>/<digest>`.

page.description: 1-based page of a captured document, for facts cited from a PDF.

RecordSource.title: RecordSource
RecordSource.description: The registry's record of where one row version came from. `origin` is `roster` for a row built from a roster file, or `resolution` for a row created by entity resolution.

origin.description: Whether the version came from a roster capture or from entity resolution.

source_key.description: The roster's collector key, for roster rows.

capture_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the roster capture, for roster rows.

row_number.description: 1-based row in the roster capture, for roster rows.

Identifier.title: Identifier
Identifier.description: An external identifier an issuer gives an entity, such as a CRA business number (namespace ca.cra.bn9) or a StatCan census subdivision code (ca.statcan.csd_uid). Resolve any identifier to its entities with GET /v1/identifiers/{namespace}/{value}.

value.description: The identifier exactly as its issuer writes it.

vintage.description: The edition of the code list the identifier belongs to, such as a census year.

valid_from.description: When the entity started holding the identifier, at the source's precision. Null when unknown.

valid_to.description: When the entity stopped holding the identifier. Null when it still does or the source gives no end.

provenance.description: Where this identifier version came from.

Predicate.title: Predicate
Predicate.description: The kind of relationship, read as "subject <predicate> object": governs, located_within, covers, party_to, administrative_part_of, reports_to_minister, owned_by, controlled_by, member_of, succeeded_by. Person predicates (director_of, has_significant_control_over) arrive in phase 2 under read:persons. New predicates may be added.

Relationship.title: Relationship
Relationship.description: A dated, cited relationship between an entity (the subject) and another entity or a non-entity object, such as "Town of Diamond Valley located_within census subdivision 4806014" or "Department A succeeded_by Department B". Exactly one of object_id and object_ref is set.

id.description: Identifier of this relationship version (the registry row_id). A changed relationship gets a new id; the old one stays readable in earlier releases.

subject_id.description: The entity the relationship is about.

object_id.description: The entity on the other side, or null when the object is not an entity (see object_ref).

object_ref.description: A non-entity object as `<namespace>:<value>`, such as ca.statcan.dguid:2021A00054806014, or null when the object is an entity.

object.description: The object entity, compactly, when object_id is set.

direction.description: Relative to the entity in the request path: `out` when it is the subject, `in` when it is the object.

attributes.description: Predicate-specific values, such as percent and holding_type for owned_by, or event, effective_date, authority and citations for succeeded_by. Empty object when none.

valid_from.description: When the relationship became true in the world, at the source's precision.

valid_to.description: When the relationship stopped being true, at the source's precision. Null when still true or unknown.

provenance.description: Where this relationship version came from.

cite.description: A ready-to-paste citation for this relationship.

SourceKey.description: The spending source: the fact-factory adapter that collected the row. Each source has its own meaning of `amount`, of `fiscal_year` and of revisions; read GET /v1/spending/sources before comparing or totalling. New sources may be added.

SpendingRecordGid.title: SpendingRecordGid
SpendingRecordGid.description: Global ID of one published spending row: `gid://buildcanada/SpendingRecord/` followed by its 26-character spending key. The key is the first 128 bits of sha256(asset_key, acquisition, resource_id, id), written in Crockford base32. It is stable for as long as the source row exists, across releases.

Amount.title: Amount
Amount.description: A monetary amount as a decimal string, never a float, such as "125000.00". At least two and at most six decimal places. Negative values are published as the source gives them (for example recoveries). The currency is in the sibling `currency` field.

CurrencyCode.title: CurrencyCode
CurrencyCode.description: An ISO 4217 currency code. CAD for every source except global_affairs_projects.

Measure.title: Measure
Measure.description: What a source's `amount` measures. Amounts of different measures are different quantities and must never be added together. contract_value: a contract's reported value, not payments. aggregated_contract_value: a total of small contracts and acquisition-card spending. agreement_value: a grant or contribution agreement's value, not money paid. payments_or_expenditure: transfer payments, either aggregate payments or current-year expenditure (the source does not record which). award_amount: a research award. commitment: international development commitments, not spending.

SpendingParty.title: SpendingParty
SpendingParty.description: One party named on a spending row (one occurrence), and whether and why it is linked to a registry entity. `link_status` is linked (an active rule linked it), proposed (a rule matched but is not yet active, so the entity is only the first candidate) or unlinked (see reason). Never treat proposed as linked.

occurrence_id.description: One party on one spending row. Stable across releases.

field.description: Which party field of the row the occurrence came from.

position.description: 0-based position within a list field (recipients); 0 for single-valued fields.

raw_name.description: The party's name exactly as the row publishes it.

normalized_name.description: raw_name after the registry's versioned name normalization (accents and punctuation removed, casefolded, legal-form suffixes dropped).

party_kind.description: Whether the party is an organization, an individual, an aggregate of many recipients, or unknown. Individuals are never linked in phase 1.

link_status.description: linked, proposed or unlinked, as above. Derived from entity_id and reason.

entity_id.description: The linked entity, or null when not linked.

entity.description: The linked entity, compactly, or null.

method.description: The rule that linked the occurrence, or that proposed a link when link_status is proposed. Null when no rule matched.

reason.description: Why the occurrence is not linked. Null when linked. Look each value up with GET /v1/dictionary/reason.

candidates.description: Entity gids (or `ca/ised/federal_corporations:<number>` anchors for corporations not yet entities) the rules found for an unlinked occurrence. For proposed, the proposed entity is first. Empty when linked or when there are none.

rule_version.description: The resolution, extraction, normalization and matching versions that produced this outcome.

SpendingRecordListResponse.title: SpendingRecordListResponse
SpendingRecordListResponse.description: A page of spending rows. The standard list envelope: items in `data`, the cursor for the next page in `meta.next_cursor` and `links.next`.

data.description: A page of spending rows.

meta.description: The release that answered, the resolved as_of, the request ID, caveats and pagination.

links.description: Links for this page and the next.

SpendingSummaryRow.title: SpendingSummaryRow
SpendingSummaryRow.description: One group of an entity's linked spending. Rows are always split by source (and by currency), because sources measure different things and overlap: never add amounts of rows with different sources. Within a source, only the highest-ranked revision per canonical_id is summed, aggregate rows are left out, and blank amounts are counted in amount_missing, never as zero.

source.description: The spending source. Always a grouping key.

fiscal_year.description: The fiscal year, when grouped by fiscal_year; otherwise null.

counterparty.description: The entity on the other side (the payer for role=recipient, the recipient for role=payer), when grouped by counterparty; otherwise null. Unlinked counterparties are grouped under null with group_by=counterparty.

records.description: Rows counted (latest revisions only, aggregates excluded).

agreements.description: Distinct canonical_id values among the counted rows.

amount.description: Sum of amount over the counted rows with an amount. Its meaning is the source's measure.

amount_missing.description: Counted rows whose amount is blank. They add nothing to amount; a large value means amount understates the group.

currency.description: The currency of amount. A source with several currencies gets one row per currency.

measure.description: What amount measures, from the source.

SpendingSummaryResponse.title: SpendingSummaryResponse
SpendingSummaryResponse.description: An entity's linked spending, grouped. Not paginated: there is one row per group, at most a few thousand. `meta.caveats` always includes not_cross_source_total, latest_revision_only and linked_only.

data.description: One row per group. Never add amounts across rows with different sources.

meta.description: Standard meta plus what the summary left out.

role.description: The role the entity was summarized in.

group_by.description: The grouping keys used. `source` is always included.

aggregated_rows_excluded.description: Linked aggregate rows (is_aggregated) left out of every group.

unlinked_occurrences.description: Unlinked occurrences in the same role that carry the entity's normalized name or an alias. Not counted in any group; list them with /v1/entities/{id}/spending/unlinked.

links.description: Links for the summary.

unlinked.description: The unlinked occurrences counted in meta.

SpendingRecordRef.title: SpendingRecordRef
SpendingRecordRef.description: A compact reference to a spending row. Fetch the full row from its `id`.

fiscal_year.description: The fiscal year the row belongs to, by the source's rule.

amount.description: The row's amount; see the source's measure. Null when the source gives no single value.

payer.description: The paying government organization as the source names it.

title.description: Short name of the contract, agreement, award or project.

UnlinkedOccurrence.title: UnlinkedOccurrence
UnlinkedOccurrence.description: A spending party occurrence that is not linked to the entity but carries the entity's normalized name or one of its aliases: a candidate the reader may want to check. It is not counted in the entity's spending or summary.

party.description: The occurrence, with its reason and candidates.

record.description: The row the occurrence is on.

UnlinkedOccurrenceListResponse.title: UnlinkedOccurrenceListResponse
UnlinkedOccurrenceListResponse.description: A page of unlinked occurrences that carry the entity's name. The standard list envelope: items in `data`, the cursor for the next page in `meta.next_cursor` and `links.next`.

data.description: A page of unlinked occurrences that carry the entity's name.

meta.description: The release that answered, the resolved as_of, the request ID, caveats and pagination.

links.description: Links for this page and the next.

IdentifierMatch.title: IdentifierMatch
IdentifierMatch.description: One entity that holds a resolved identifier, with the identifier row that says so.

identifier.description: The identifier row, with its provenance.

IdentifierResolution.title: IdentifierResolution
IdentifierResolution.description: The result of resolving an external identifier. Usually one entity holds it; several can (for example an amalgamated corporation's predecessors share its BN), and the caller decides which applies, often by `valid_from` and `valid_to`.

value.description: The value as the issuer writes it, after the API removed spaces and, for business numbers, the program account suffix.

matches.description: Every entity holding the identifier in the release that answered.

IdentifierResolutionResponse.title: IdentifierResolutionResponse
IdentifierResolutionResponse.description: The entities holding an identifier. The standard envelope: the object in `data`, facts about the response in `meta`, and a pinned `self` link.

data.description: The entities holding an identifier.

meta.description: The release that answered, the resolved as_of, the request ID and caveats.

links.description: Links for the response.

SpendingSource.title: SpendingSource
SpendingSource.description: What one spending source's rows mean: its measure, how `amount`, `fiscal_year` and revisions work, its coverage, licence and the snapshot the release pinned. Read this before comparing or totalling amounts. Amounts from different sources overlap (the same grant can appear in proactive_grants and in transfer_payments) and must never be added.

asset.description: The fact-factory asset key of the source's Iceberg table.

title.description: The publisher's name for the dataset.
examples: Proactive Disclosure of Grants and Contributions

publisher.description: The organization that publishes the source.

record_types.description: The record types the source publishes.

amount_note.description: Which source field fills amount, and its known defects.
examples: agreement_value for that amendment. Do not sum across rows sharing a canonical_id.

fiscal_year_note.description: How the source's fiscal_year is derived.
examples: The fiscal year (April to March) containing agreement_start_date, named by the calendar year it starts in.

revisions_note.description: How the source's canonical_id groups revisions, or that it has none.
examples: Hash of owner_org and ref_number. Each amendment is its own row.

license.description: The publisher's licence for the source.

snapshot_id.description: The Iceberg snapshot of the source table this release pinned.

caveats.description: Caveats that always apply to this source.

links.description: Relative links for the source.

SpendingSourceListResponse.title: SpendingSourceListResponse
SpendingSourceListResponse.description: Every spending source and what its amounts mean. The standard list envelope: items in `data`, the cursor for the next page in `meta.next_cursor` and `links.next`.

data.description: Every spending source and what its amounts mean.

meta.description: The release that answered, the resolved as_of, the request ID, caveats and pagination.

links.description: Links for this page and the next.

SpendingRecordResponse.title: SpendingRecordResponse
SpendingRecordResponse.description: One spending row. The standard envelope: the object in `data`, facts about the response in `meta`, and a pinned `self` link.

data.description: One spending row.

meta.description: The release that answered, the resolved as_of, the request ID and caveats.

links.description: Links for the response.

ExportListResponse.title: ExportListResponse
ExportListResponse.description: A page of bulk files. The standard list envelope: items in `data`, the cursor for the next page in `meta.next_cursor` and `links.next`.

data.description: A page of bulk files.

meta.description: The release that answered, the resolved as_of, the request ID, caveats and pagination.

links.description: Links for this page and the next.

CacheControl.description: `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` when the request pinned `as_of`; otherwise `public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600`. Responses for /me, /me/usage and `count=exact` are `private, no-store`.

RateLimit.description: The caller's remaining units in the current window, per draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers: `r` is units remaining and `t` seconds until the window resets.

RateLimitPolicy.description: The caller's limits: `q` is the quota in units and `w` the window in seconds, for the per-minute rate and the monthly (or, for anonymous callers, daily) allowance.

QuotaRemaining.description: Units left in the caller's monthly (anonymous, daily) allowance.

WWWAuthenticate.description: RFC 6750 challenge. On 401 it names the protected-resource metadata (`Bearer resource_metadata="https://data.buildcanada.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`); on 403 it names the missing scope (`Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="read:persons"`).

ETag.description: A strong validator for the response, `"r<release>-<first 12 hex of sha256>"`. Send it back as If-None-Match for a free 304.

BCRelease.description: The release that answered, the same as `meta.release`. Absent for data versioned only by time.

Location.description: The survivor entity's URL, pinned to the same release.

BadRequest.description: invalid_parameter: a parameter is malformed, unknown or out of range. `errors` names each one.

value.title: Invalid parameter
value.detail: fiscal_year must be a fiscal year label.

Unauthorized.description: unauthenticated: the key or token is missing where one is needed, unknown, revoked or expired.

unauthenticated.summary: No key on an operation that needs one

value.title: Authentication required
value.detail: This operation needs an API key or OAuth token. Get a free key at https://auth.buildcanada.com/developers.

Forbidden.description: insufficient_scope: the key or token lacks the scope in `required_scope`. account_suspended: the account that owns the key is suspended. ip_not_allowed and origin_not_allowed: the key is restricted to other IP addresses or origins.

value.title: Insufficient scope
value.detail: This key does not have the usage:read scope.

TooManyRequests.description: rate_limited: wait `retry_after_seconds`. quota_exceeded: the month is spent; upgrade or use bulk files.

value.title: Rate limit exceeded
value.detail: Key bc_live_7Hq2… used 120 of 120 request units in the current 60-second window.

value.title: Monthly quota exceeded
value.detail: Account acct_42 used 100,000 of 100,000 units this month. The quota resets on 2026-10-01.

InternalError.description: internal_error: an unexpected failure. Retry once; quote `instance` if it persists.

value.title: Internal error
value.detail: Something went wrong on our side. Quote req_01JA8X3M2Q9R4T6V8W0Y2Z4B6C if it happens again.

ServiceUnavailable.description: release_building: the read model is switching to a new release. Retry after Retry-After seconds, or pin `as_of`.

value.title: Release building
value.detail: Release 12 is being published. Retry in 30 seconds, or pin as_of=11.

Conflict.description: release_mismatch: the cursor was issued for another release than `as_of`.

value.title: Cursor from another release
value.detail: This cursor belongs to release 10. Repeat with as_of=10, or drop the cursor to start again.

NotModified.description: The If-None-Match ETag still matches. No body. Costs 0 units but counts toward the request rate.

NotFound.description: not_found: nothing has this ID in the release that answered. not_yet_published: `as_of` is before the first release.

UnprocessableEntity.description: query_too_broad: the query would exceed the search, graph or grouping limits, or took longer than the statement timeout. Narrow it, or use bulk files.

query_too_broad.summary: A search query that is too short

value.title: Query too broad
value.detail: q must have at least 2 characters other than spaces and punctuation.

MovedPermanently.description: redirected: the entity was merged into a survivor. Follow Location; the old ID keeps working.

value.title: Entity redirected
value.detail: Entity 01J9ZK4T6M8Q2R5V7X3B1N0C4D was merged into 01JB2C3D4E5F6G7H8J9K0M1N2P in release 11.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Items per page, 1 to 200. Default 50. Pages over 50 cost 2 units instead of 1.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The opaque `meta.next_cursor` of the previous page. Send it with the same other parameters. A cursor carries its release, so pages stay consistent even after a newer release publishes; sending it with a different `as_of` returns 409 release_mismatch.

AcceptLanguage.name: Accept-Language
AcceptLanguage.description: Set to `fr` for French `cite` and caveat `text`. Data values are never translated; `name_fr` carries French names.

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description: An ETag from an earlier response. When it still matches, the API answers 304 Not Modified, which costs no units.

AsOf.name: as_of
AsOf.description: Pins the answer to a point in the data's history, so the same URL returns the same bytes forever. A release number (`11`) pins that release. An RFC 3339 timestamp (`2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`) or a date (`2026-09-01`, read as 00:00 UTC) resolves to the release current at that time. Omitted means the latest release, which the response names in `meta.release` and in its `self` link; pass that back to reproduce it. A value before the first release returns 404 not_yet_published.

timestamp.summary: The release current at a time

ValidOn.name: valid_on
ValidOn.description: Only items true in the world on this date: valid_from on or before it (or blank) and valid_to after it (or blank). This is real-world time; `as_of` is data history.

Fields.name: fields
Fields.description: Comma-separated top-level fields of each item to return, such as `id,name,status`. `id` and `cite` are always returned. Unknown names return 400 invalid_parameter.

Count.name: count
Count.description: Set to `exact` to return the total in `meta.count`. Costs 2 more units. Omit it when paging.

EntityId.name: id
EntityId.description: The entity: its bare 26-character ULID, or its percent-encoded global ID (`gid%3A%2F%2Fbuildcanada%2FEntity%2F01J9ZK4T6M8Q2R5V7X3B1N0C4D`).

SpendingRole.name: role
SpendingRole.description: The entity's role on the rows. `recipient` (default) or `payer`.

SpendingSource.name: source
SpendingSource.description: Only rows of these sources, comma-separated. Amounts of different sources overlap; never add them.

FiscalYear.name: fiscal_year
FiscalYear.description: Only rows of this Government of Canada fiscal year, as `YYYY-YY` (`2024-25` is April 2024 to March 2025).
